title: A Bakery for the Tide
premise: Beatrix Whitlock has spent twelve years hiding behind the counter of her bookshop, raising her daughter and answering a decade of anonymous letters left in her drop box—letters signed only 'T.' When the letters stop and a stranger named Tomas Alder buys the derelict bakery next door, Beatrix discovers he is her correspondent, a former journalist who fled the coastal town of Saltmere after exposing a corruption scandal that ruined him and, she learns, was entangled with the disappearance of her sister years ago. As their slow-burn romance deepens, Beatrix must choose between the safe, small life she built and the dangerous truth Tomas still carries—a truth the town's powerful Harrow family will do anything to bury. In the end, Beatrix publishes the evidence herself through her bookshop's press, Tomas testifies at great personal cost, and the two of them, scarred but whole, finally risk the whole heart as Saltmere's tide turns.
about_author: Juniper Winterbourne is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who writes love stories about people who mend broken things. She lives on the coast with a stubborn cat and an ever-growing stack of unsent letters.

chapters.title: The Drop Box
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. On a rainy Tuesday, Beatrix opens her bookshop's after-hours drop box and finds the eleventh annual letter from 'T.'—a confession of love she's never answered. She reads it twice, hides it with the others, and pretends her heart didn't lurch. Emotional beat: longing disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Flour and Dust
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A moving van arrives at the abandoned bakery next door. Beatrix meets Tomas Alder—wary, charming, hands dusted with flour—and feels an unsettling flicker of recognition. Her daughter Wren immediately adopts him. Emotional beat: curiosity edged with dread.

chapters.title: Twelve Safe Years
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A flashback chapter: the scandal that drove her from journalism, her sister Maren's disappearance, and the small life she built brick by brick. Beatrix reminds herself why she never risks anything. Emotional beat: the architecture of fear.

chapters.title: The Last Letter
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas unpacks boxes in the bakery and rereads the final letter he never sent—the one explaining who he really is. He came to Saltmere not for bread but for Maren Whitlock's file, and for the woman he's loved through the mail for a decade. Emotional beat: guilt braided with hope.

chapters.title: Closing Time
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A power outage traps Beatrix and Tomas in the bookshop after hours. Candlelight, wine, and a conversation that skirts the edges of everything unsaid. He quotes a line from one of her favorite novels—the same phrasing from the letters. Emotional beat: intimacy arriving too fast.

chapters.title: The Harrows of Saltmere
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Councilman Edwin Harrow visits the bakery with a smile and a warning: Saltmere doesn't like outsiders digging. Tomas recognizes the name from his investigation—Harrow's development company owned the pier where Maren was last seen. Emotional beat: the past sharpening its teeth.

chapters.title: What Wren Knows
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Wren, now twelve, admits she found the letters years ago and has been leaving them in the drop box herself—she thought 'T.' was a ghost. Mother and daughter argue about secrets, and Beatrix realizes her silence has been its own kind of lie. Emotional beat: the cost of protection.

chapters.title: Bread at Dawn
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas teaches Wren to knead dough while Beatrix watches from the doorway. For one morning, they are almost a family, and Tomas nearly tells her the truth. Instead he asks her about Maren—and watches her shut down. Emotional beat: warmth undercut by the approaching reveal.

chapters.title: The Eleventh Letter, Signed
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix finds an unsigned draft in Tomas's bakery office—her letter, word for word. Confronted, Tomas confesses everything except the part about Maren: he is 'T.,' he loved her from afar, he moved here for her. Beatrix flees, feeling seen and betrayed at once. Emotional beat: the floor giving way.

chapters.title: Half a Truth
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas tracks Beatrix to the sea wall and tells her the rest: he was the journalist whose exposé of the Harrow pier collapse led to Maren's disappearance—she was his source. He came to finish what she started. Beatrix's grief turns to fury, then to a terrible resolve. Emotional beat: rage becoming partnership.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix weighs loyalty—to her daughter's safety, to Maren's memory, to the town that sheltered her—against the truth Tomas carries. She agrees to help him, but on her terms: no more secrets between them, ever. Their first real kiss happens in the rain. Emotional beat: alliance becoming love.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. In the newspaper archive, Tomas and Beatrix reconstruct Maren's final weeks: she'd found proof the Harrows knowingly built the pier on faulty pilings. The last entry in her notes is a meeting she never returned from. Emotional beat: hope and horror in the same box.

chapters.title: An Old Friend's Price
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix approaches Ruth Calloway, the retired police clerk who filed Maren's case, and finds her terrified—someone has been paying her silence for twelve years. Ruth gives Beatrix a key to a storage unit and begs her to stop. Emotional beat: the town's complicity surfacing.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The storage unit holds Maren's hidden evidence—documents, photos, and a tape naming Edwin Harrow directly. That night, the bakery is broken into and ransacked; Tomas is beaten and warned. Beatrix stitches his split brow by lamplight. Emotional beat: love declared in the language of care.

chapters.title: The Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix and Tomas finally speak plainly: not pieces, not letters, but everything—her fear of losing another person, his shame over Maren. They commit to each other and to publishing the truth, knowing the Harrows will come for them. Emotional beat: the vow beneath the romance.

chapters.title: Pressure
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The Harrows escalate: the bookshop's lease is challenged, Wren is followed home from school, and an offer of money arrives with an implicit threat. Tomas considers running with Beatrix and Wren to protect them—and hates himself for considering it. Emotional beat: the temptation of escape.

chapters.title: Wren's Choice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, having pieced together that 'T.' is the baker and that the truth involves her Aunt Maren, confronts her mother: 'She was mine too. You don't get to decide alone.' Beatrix sees Maren's stubbornness in her daughter and finally stops treating Wren as something to shelter. Emotional beat: family redefined as honesty.

chapters.title: The Print Run
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Using the bookshop's old letterpress, Beatrix, Tomas, Wren, and Ruth print five hundred copies of Maren's evidence overnight—'The Saltmere Truth,' with the tape transcribed. At dawn they slip copies into every mailbox on the coast. Emotional beat: quiet, trembling defiance.

chapters.title: The Meeting at the Pier
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Edwin Harrow corners Tomas at the ruined pier with two men and an ultimatum. Tomas, expecting it, has been recording since he arrived; Beatrix and the sheriff—Ruth's nephew, finally shown the tape—arrive before it becomes a second disappearance. Emotional beat: the trap reversed.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Tomas testifies before the state investigation, sacrificing his anonymity and any hope of a quiet life. Beatrix watches from the gallery, Wren's hand in hers, as the Harrow empire cracks in public. Edwin is indicted; the pier file is reopened as a homicide. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, then inside it.

chapters.title: What Maren Would Have Said
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A memorial on the rebuilt pier: Maren's name carved into the new railing, Wren reading her aunt's last letter aloud to the whole town. Beatrix forgives Tomas fully—not for Maren's death, but for the years they both spent afraid. Emotional beat: grief transformed into inheritance.

chapters.title: A Bakery for the Tide
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. One year later: the bakery opens its doors, the bookshop publishes its first real title under Maren's name, and Beatrix leaves a letter in her own drop box—signed, this time, with her whole name. Tomas reads it on the doorstep and comes inside. Emotional beat: the tide coming in, and staying.
